## What the data says
- Thin fabric has no PSI microgravity test data at 10.2 psia / 26.5 % O₂; the nearest tests are at 17-30 % O₂ and 50.7-304 kPa [PSI-68].
- Thin solid has no PSI microgravity test data at these conditions; the closest tests are at 13.6-22.2 % O₂ and 101.3 kPa [PSI-25].
- Thick solid has no PSI microgravity test data at these conditions; the nearest tests are at 13.6-22.2 % O₂ and 101.3 kPa [PSI-25].
- Liquid fuel droplets (methanol, n-heptane) have 8 nearby PSI microgravity test runs that all sustained burning at 30 % O₂ and 71.2-102.5 kPa, 0 cm/s flow; 100 % of these runs kept burning [PSI-69].
- Fire-resistant materials (silicone, Nomex) have 8 PSI microgravity runs at ≤22.2 % O₂; 3 kept burning and 5 did not (3 Nomex, 4 silicone) [PSI-25] [PSI-99].
- Nomex HT90-40 failed NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 at 30 % O₂ and 70.1 kPa in 1 g (NTRS 20070018178).
- Partial-gravity combustion data are absent; NASA FM2 researchers note that flame spread may be most hazardous near lunar gravity (NTRS 20260000646).

## How confident we can be
- Solid data are dominated by sustained runs: 131 of 134 ordinary solid tests sustained burning; only 2 extinction-velocity limits and 1 no-ignition run exist, so a flammability limit cannot be located [PSI-25] [PSI-98][PSI-99].
- Fire-resistant material data show mixed results; 3 of 8 runs sustained burning, indicating no clear safety margin at ≤22.2 % O₂ [PSI-25] [PSI-99].
- Droplet data provide evidence coverage of 0.545 for methanol and n-heptane at the target conditions, all sustained [PSI-69].
- No test data exist for thin or thick solids at the target atmosphere; physics estimates place flame temperatures 130-140 K above the hottest tested condition, but these are not measurements [PSI-68] [PSI-25].

## Gaps
- No PSI microgravity test runs for thin fabric, thin solid, or thick solid at 10.2 psia / 26.5 % O₂; physics estimates only.
- Partial-gravity combustion data are missing; microgravity and 1-g results do not bound lunar or Martian gravity (NTRS 20260000646).
- Fire-resistant materials lack data at higher oxygen levels (≥26.5 % O₂) and higher pressures; only ≤22.2 % O₂ tests exist.
- No data on flame spread rates or quenching speeds for thin fabrics in the target atmosphere.

## What future experiments (e.g. LUCI, FM2) should measure
- Thin fabric combustion at 10.2 psia / 26.5 % O₂, 70.3 kPa, 0 cm/s flow, recording flame temperature, spread rate, and extinction behavior.
- Thin solid and thick solid tests at the same conditions, with varied flow speeds to assess quenching boundaries.
- Fire-resistant materials (silicone, Nomex) at ≥26.5 % O₂ and 70.3 kPa to determine ignition thresholds and sustained burn characteristics.
- Partial-gravity (≈0.166 g) combustion experiments for all material classes to evaluate whether flame spread is more hazardous than in microgravity or 1-g.
- Droplet tests at 26.5 % O₂ and 70.3 kPa with varied flow to refine physics estimates and confirm sustained burning margins.
